task.title: Blend elements
task.shortdesc: A blend mode chooses how the colors of an element mix with the colors under it. You can also isolate a group so that its elements blend with each other and not with what is behind the group.

info.p: The mix-blend-mode property sets the blend mode of an element. The initial value is normal, which paints the element over what is behind it. You can set a mode on shapes, text, images, groups and use elements. On a group, the mode applies to the group as one picture.
The modes are those of the PDF format:

row.entry: Multiplies the colors. The result is never lighter. Multiplying by white changes nothing.
Multiplies the opposite of the colors. The result is never darker. Screening with black changes nothing.
Multiplies dark colors of the backdrop and screens light ones.
Keep the darker or the lighter of the two colors in each channel.
Brighten or darken the backdrop to reflect the color of the element.
Multiply or screen, depending on the color of the element. The effect is harsh with hard-light and gentle with soft-light.
Subtract the darker color from the lighter one. exclusion has less contrast.
Take the named part of the color from the element and the other parts from the backdrop. color takes the hue and the saturation.

fig.title: A red circle over a blue and yellow backdrop in each blend mode

image.alt: Sixteen small rectangles, half blue and half yellow, each with a red circle on top. The circle looks different in each one, depending on the blend mode named under it. The last one is the normal mode.

info.p: An element blends with everything painted before it in the same group. A group is isolated when its elements blend with each other and nothing outside the group takes part. With isolation: isolate you make a group isolated. The initial value is auto.
A group is isolated by itself, without the property, when it has an opacity below 1, a clip-path or a mask, because CSSMedia paints such a group as one picture first.
